label: VTS0 — Visibility-Topology Scheduler feasibility audit
question: Does topology-aware dependency scheduling provide additional safe optimizer skipping beyond visibility-based VOS?

execution.method: zero-diff visibility + topology trace on frozen C0

structural_argument: VOS already skips all invisible rows (visibility_skip_ratio 0.62-0.75).
A visible row has a real nonzero gradient; its Adam transition is real and skipping it changes the trajectory (not exact). Topology cannot zero a visible row's gradient.
Topology events (clone/split/prune) only ADD forced reads/copies/settlements; they never enable skipping a visible row's real step. topology_forced/lineage/settlement ratios are COSTS.
In the VOS active region (iter 15001..30000) topology is FROZEN (densify_until_iter=15000 gates clone/split/prune and opacity reset), so all topology ratios are exactly 0 there.
Therefore extra_safe_skip_headroom = 0 in the VOS region; in the dynamic region topology only REDUCES headroom.
why_killed: Topology-awareness provides zero additional safe optimizer skipping beyond visibility. Invisibility is the only exact skip signal (zero-grad => exact deferred replay); topology is a forced-cost channel.
what_must_not_be_revived: Any claim that topology-aware dependency scheduling adds optimizer-skipping headroom beyond visibility. Reviving requires a new mechanism making a visible row's optimizer step provably redundant (would break exactness).
